topic: Explain first in, first out using a queue at a tiny ticket booth. Show three numbered visitors arriving and leaving in order. Make the rule visible with a simple diagram, then return to the booth for the payoff.
visualDirection: An original teal-jacketed presenter, warm paper backgrounds and coral accents. Keep the same presenter proportions, face and colors across cuts.

lines.text: Why does a queue work? Meet three visitors waiting for tickets at our tiny booth.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The first visitor joins the front. The second waits behind, and the third joins last.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: When the booth opens, the visitor at the front gets a ticket and leaves first.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The others move forward, keeping their order. New arrivals always join the back of this queue.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: That rule is first in, first out. Our diagram follows the same order as the visitors.
lines.speaker: narrator

shotPlan.picture: Medium view of the booth. The original presenter raises an open palm in a questioning pose, looking from the viewer to three waiting visitors. One short physical sign reads TICKETS.

Cut to a board closeup to isolate the arrival order. Three numbered tokens enter in order, 1 then 2 then 3. The presenter points to token 1 with gaze following the fingertip. Sparse labels read FRONT and BACK.
Cut back to the booth to connect the diagram to the example. Visitor 1 receives a ticket and leaves; 2 and 3 remain in their original order. The presenter turns to follow visitor 1.
Diagram closeup makes the change legible. Token 1 exits, 2 and 3 advance together without swapping, and token 4 joins the back. Reveal each movement on its corresponding narration phrase.

A wider callback reconnects booth and diagram. The same presenter reacts with a small smile and open hand toward the matching visitor/token order. A physical board reads FIRST IN / FIRST OUT, with all text and faces inside a 10% inset.
